records.name: Analytical versus clinical validation
records.tldr: Analytical validity concerns whether a test measures reliably. Clinical validity concerns what its result means for a condition or outcome. Clinical utility concerns using that information for a decision.
records.summary: Analytical validity, clinical validity and clinical utility address different questions for a specified assay, specimen, population and intended use. MedlinePlus Genetics distinguishes detection of a genetic variant, its relationship to disease presence or risk, and whether the information helps diagnosis, treatment, management or prevention. Reliable measurement does not by itself establish clinical meaning, and an outcome association does not establish benefit from changing care. For a prediction model, reproducibility of fixed-input output, discrimination, calibrated probabilities and the consequences of model-guided decisions also require distinct evidence. These are related questions rather than a universal sequence that guarantees a useful test.

notes: Start a claim worksheet with the population and treatment setting, specimen and method version, measured or predicted outcome, time horizon and proposed decision. A molecule measurement, drug ranking in a dish and outcome prediction from earlier patients are different claims. For risk, retain whether the estimate assumes usual care or no treatment; for a drug experiment, retain the drug, dose and combination. Leave unavailable details unknown. Then separate the tested material and quality, biological interpretation and alternatives, prediction, proposed action and evidence of benefit. Mark each measured, inferred, proposed or unknown. A sound measurement does not automatically support the later steps.

Consider a fictional report that calls a protein-rich stored tumour a Drug A responder. Its study related protein abundance to shrinkage among people all receiving Drug A for advanced Cancer X. The measurement and response association can be useful, but there is no untreated or alternative-treatment comparison establishing greater benefit from A. Applying it after surgery also changes the setting. Ask what comparison shows improved outcomes from choosing A with this result in the proposed setting. Confirmation of protein abundance answers whether that signal is real, while postoperative benefit remains a separate question. A favourable prognostic result does not itself justify omitting standard treatment.

An evidence card records population, stage, treatment context and selection; specimen, handling, assay version and quality criteria; the reference condition or care comparator and its limitations; outcome and measurement time; the analysis plan, all tuning and independent evaluation; failed samples, dropout and missing outcomes; and sample size, intervals and remaining uncertainty. A response endpoint is not recurrence or survival. A preclinical card names the actual model and tested claim; an observational clinical association retains possible confounding. Neither alone establishes that the proposed clinical action helps. A headline metric also needs the consequences of false positive and false negative calls attached to the action. Distinguish prespecified analyses from exploratory searches, keep their tuning history, and seek confirmation that does not reuse the search. State whether a treatment-study denominator includes everyone assigned, only those treated or only those evaluable.

For analytical performance, request the detection limit with its target level, input amount, specimen and detection probability; precision within runs and across days, operators, instruments and reagent lots; agreement with an appropriate independent reference; attempted-sample failure rate and reasons; and specimen handling, preservation and interference testing. The 2017 AMP/CAP recommendations concern next-generation sequencing panels for somatic variants. They ask for performance by variant class and relevant reference materials, depth and sample numbers. They describe a lower detection limit at which 95 per cent of samples are reliably detected, but also explain why observing 19 or 20 successes in 20 trials does not by itself establish that reliability with confidence. This is an assay-specific example, not a universal validation protocol. Fresh and delayed specimens can differ, and measurement variation must be understood before interpreting a trend. Self-agreement alone does not establish accuracy.

Put the decision before ordering. Write what positive, negative, uncertain and failed results would change, including proposed treatment omission, confirmation or another sample. Compare existing pathology and other tests, and record the decision deadline, finite tissue, time, travel, uncertainty and financial burden. Name who interprets the result, who owns the clinical recommendation and when further testing is unlikely to help that decision. A result arriving after the decision closes may not serve its intended use. The worksheet exposes assumptions rather than calculating a treatment choice; urgency does not establish validity.

In the fictional postoperative protein-test case, possible next steps are checking the actual companion-diagnostic requirement and whether this assay meets it, inspecting the Drug A evidence, considering a trial of the relevant strategy, or declining a tissue-consuming test that would not change the decision. The exact laboratory, service, version and intended use matter. A research-use label, laboratory certification, development designation or report drug list cannot replace the claim-specific evidence. A companion test is tied to specified treatment use. Clinician-led off-label use, access, payment and suitability are additional questions, not promises made by a molecular report. Fast-track and breakthrough-therapy designations are not marketing approval; accelerated approval is a distinct approval pathway, not just a development designation.

Research can have a defined value without selecting treatment: checking a mechanism, explaining discordant assays or generating a future hypothesis. Name the reviewer and what would count as a useful answer rather than extending an endless chain of tests. Attribute unpublished company data and state which methods and results were available to inspect; unavailable evidence does not prove the claim false. In a fictional high/low recurrence-risk test for which neither answer changes recommended care and no relevant study is open, the immediate value for that treatment decision is limited. A separate research or personal-information goal should be weighed against burden, uncertainty and alternatives. A changed treatment decision is not itself demonstrated benefit and can add unnecessary treatment.

records.name: Bioprinting of experimental tissue models
records.tldr: Bioprinting places cells or materials in a planned arrangement; the constructed tissue still needs structural and functional checks.
records.summary: Bioprinting controls deposition of biological materials to build an experimental construct. The printing plan, measured final geometry, viable cells and biological function are distinct evidence. Kolesky and colleagues printed cell-containing and removable inks, removed the temporary channel material, added endothelial lining and perfused engineered tissues. This tissue-engineering experiment did not demonstrate a complete human organ or cancer-treatment utility. Yi and colleagues reported a particular glioblastoma chip combining patient-derived tumour cells, endothelial cells and brain-derived matrix; its abstract supports that bounded example.

links.label: Kolesky et al. 2016 primary fabrication and channel checks
Yi et al. 2019 primary abstract

notes: Model card. Input: defined cells and biomaterials, sometimes viable patient-derived material requiring expansion. Document the source of each component; patient-derived tumour cells do not make every material donor-matched. Fabrication and quality checks consume finite material. Output: measured geometry in micrometres or millimetres, viability or attributed counts, and the separately chosen functional endpoint. Retain actual layout, matrix, cell identities, time and controls; a digital plan is not the final measurement. A printing plan specifies positions, materials and fabrication steps. A bioink is a formulation used to build a biological construct, often containing cells in a supportive material. The extracellular matrix is the surrounding molecular scaffold of tissue; a printing material represents selected features rather than its whole composition. A sacrificial ink is temporary material removed to leave a channel. Some designs deposit cells with the material; another route builds a support that is seeded afterwards. Gelation, adding cell populations and making channels are distinct steps. Kolesky's cell-laden and fugitive-ink method is one documented implementation, rather than proof of every possible printing route. Source: https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1521342113

Channel checks. A temporary channel path becomes a hollow channel after removal; endothelial lining, fluid passage and barrier performance require separate tests. Kolesky's primary figures distinguish these steps and compare diffusional permeability of lined and bare channels. Printing describes fabrication; a chip describes an environment, while organoid self-organisation describes another design axis. More complex fabrication does not automatically validate prediction. Living cells can spread, contract and remodel the initial layout. The actual geometry and cell health therefore need observation after printing as well as a design file. In Kolesky's primary PDF, figures 1 and 2 separate fabrication, viability, endothelial lining and measured permeability of lined versus bare channels. Those checks support those engineered tissues, not a complete organ. Perfusion supplies fluid through the constructed system; it is not full human circulation or drug metabolism.

Fictional reading exercise. Growth changes when both gel composition and neighbour distance change. The comparison does not isolate proximity. Compare layouts with the same material, starting populations and exposure, and verify the final construct. Failure modes include incorrect placement, cell injury, incompatible material and inadequate transport. Acceptance criteria belong to the design; there is no universal clinical printing threshold. Unequal starting composition is another failure mode, alongside placement, compatibility, cell injury and transport. Printing alone does not establish complete tumour biology or immune recognition.
records.principle: Deposit defined cells and materials in a planned arrangement, then verify constructed geometry, cell health and the intended function.
strengths: Controls a planned starting arrangement for a defined experimental question
limitations: The constructed geometry, cell health and intended function must be measured
Fabrication alone does not establish whole-tumour biology, immune recognition or patient benefit

records.name: Case report
records.tldr: A case report describes what happened to one person or a few, which can reveal a signal or a harm but cannot show what would have happened under a different treatment.
records.summary: A case report documents a clinical course, interventions, outcomes and alternative explanations. It can reveal a signal of benefit or harm without establishing what would have happened under another approach. The CARE reporting guideline includes a timeline, diagnostic assessment, interventions, follow-up, the patient perspective and consent; complete reporting supports appraisal rather than proving treatment causation.

links.label: CARE guidelines: consensus-based clinical case reporting guideline (Deutsches Arzteblatt 2013)
CENT 2015: CONSORT extension for reporting N-of-1 trials (BMJ)

notes: A careful case timeline can preserve an unusual experience and generate questions. Published memorable successes do not supply all treated people as a denominator, so they cannot establish a response probability or treatment ranking. Several scans in one person remain observations from one person. A report usually lacks the concurrent counterfactual outcome under another treatment, and even a rigorous individual comparison would not establish the average effect in everyone sharing a cancer label.

Fictional clinical history: treatment A starts, a procedure is added, treatment B starts and a later scan improves. This establishes improvement during that course, not the separate added contributions of the procedure or B. The earlier treatment, procedure and later treatment can have overlapping lasting influences. Drawing overlapping ribbons represents that possibility and ordering only; it supplies no measured effect size or known duration. Documenting experience and planning an interpretable comparison are different routes to evidence.

A testimonial remains an attributed report until its underlying observations can be checked. In an explicitly fictional blog, a person with metastatic cancer adds an off-label medicine to standard chemotherapy and later scans show shrinkage. Accepting those observations as the example's premise establishes improvement during that combination; it does not isolate the added medicine, its safety or how often the result occurs. Record every intervention and measurement on the timeline and ask for a series or trial with all treated participants, failures, follow-up and a suitable comparison. A company video showing three successes has a different meaning if three of five or three of 500 people were treated. Selected successes do not supply the missing denominator or a personal forecast.

records.name: Cell line
records.tldr: A cell line is a population maintained through successive transfers in laboratory culture. Its identity, history and growth conditions shape what it can model.
records.summary: A cell line arises through subculture of an initial primary culture. Finite lines have limited proliferative capacity; continuous lines can proliferate for prolonged periods under suitable conditions. Continuous growth does not itself establish malignancy. Lines may attach to surfaces or grow in suspension. Their source, passage history, medium and density shape the selected population. Cancer-line strains can diverge genetically and in drug response, so a familiar name does not guarantee identical biology across laboratories.

notes: Model card. Input: documented banked cells or viable material used to establish a culture. Record source and version, medium, density, passage and relevant phenotype. Output belongs to the chosen assay, such as counts, doubling time in hours or a death fraction with its denominator. Passage counts transfers, not a fixed number of divisions. Identity matching by human short tandem repeat profiling, mycoplasma testing and phenotype/growth checks address different questions. Establishment can fail or select subsets; no line-name cutoff predicts clinical sensitivity. Sources: https://www.atcc.org/resources/culture-guides/animal-cell-culture-guide ; https://www.atcc.org/-/media/resources/technical-documents/cell-line-authentication-test-recommendations.pdf?rev=7664fa886e5948018dfe198d484bb4eb Establishing a new line uses finite viable tissue and can select populations. A cell line need not be a monolayer. ATCC uses authentication broadly for verification of identity and freedom from contamination: short tandem repeat profiling compares repeated DNA stretches to test human-line identity, while mycoplasma and other contamination tests and relevant phenotype checks answer additional questions. Passing the identity test does not answer all of them.

Fictional reading exercise. Two laboratories use the same named line with different medium and passage histories and obtain different drug responses. Check identity, contamination and matched conditions before attributing the difference to one cause. Replicate wells assess a preparation, not independent donors. Growth inhibition relative to a dividing control is not automatically killing. Sources: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6522222/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4887336/

A simple characterised line is useful for isolating a mechanism, comparing many perturbations and repeating an experiment. Its missing architecture, host drug handling and normal-tissue responses limit the inference, and a tumour-only line cannot test an immune interaction without the required added populations. A more elaborate culture changes selected ingredients; it does not create a universal hierarchy of reliability.

records.name: Cell lines as a proxy for patients
aka: cell lines as a patient proxy
records.tldr: Cancer cell lines support controlled laboratory experiments, while prediction for a patient requires separate evidence.
records.summary: Cancer cell lines are selected populations maintained in culture. Versions of the same named line can differ genetically and in drug response. The culture does not reproduce the whole tumour, host drug handling or complete immune environment. Transfer to patients therefore depends on the intended intervention, endpoint, population and validation evidence, rather than the line name alone.

notes: A result can be repeatable in one cultured population without predicting a patient outcome. The cell-line definition holds the culture, authentication and assay-reporting details; the question here is transportability. Specify which model feature, intervention and endpoint are expected to transfer to which clinical population, then test that bridge independently. Neither many wells nor a familiar line name establishes that bridge. Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6522222/

records.name: Controlled perturbation experiment
records.tldr: A controlled perturbation changes one defined factor in an experiment and compares the response with control conditions, so that the change can be told apart from background, carrier effects and assay failure.
records.summary: A controlled perturbation deliberately changes a defined factor and measures the response against appropriate comparison conditions. Vehicle, positive, negative and mechanism controls answer different questions. A reproducible response can support an experimental claim without establishing its proposed mechanism or patient benefit. Baseline growth, timing, dose and the actual unit assigned to treatment matter.

notes: A vehicle control contains the carrier without the active treatment; an untreated condition asks a different question if the carrier has effects. A positive control checks that the assay can detect a known relevant response, while a negative or non-targeting control estimates background under its design. Another independent way to disrupt the same function can support a mechanism, and a rescue restores a function to test whether that reverses the response here. Off-target effects, incomplete restoration and model context limit interpretation. These are questions for matched model, timing and readout; no one control proves specificity or patient benefit, and agreement between similar readouts is not automatically independent mechanistic confirmation.

Keep what changed, the comparator, concentration or dose range, timing, assignment, readout and units, sample identities, replicate structure and variability. Repeated wells address variation under their preparation and allocation; independently obtained biological samples address another source of variation. Many wells from one tumour do not become independent patients, and repetition or a small p-value does not repair a missing comparison. A two-drug experiment needs vehicle, both single drugs and the combination. A larger combination effect than either single drug is not automatically synergy; that claim needs a stated reference model.

Fictional direct counts: vehicle-treated cells increase from 100 to 200 while drug-treated cells remain at 100. The endpoint drug count is half the vehicle count without measured net decline from the starting count, so calling it 50 per cent killing overstates the observation. Slower growth, death and a molecular change require their own readouts; direct death or recovery measurements could address further questions. Hafner and colleagues showed that conventional IC50 and maximal-effect measures depend on cell divisions during an assay and developed growth-rate metrics to address that dependence. A real experimental response does not by itself establish the responsible target or clinical benefit.

A fictional two-drug table normalises remaining viability to vehicle at 100 per cent: A leaves 70, B leaves 80, and combination examples leave 56 or 30. Highest single agent uses the better single-drug effect, a 70 per cent remaining-viability reference here. Bliss independence predicts 0.70 times 0.80 = 0.56, or 56 per cent. Both combinations exceed the HSA effect; 56 matches Bliss while 30 exceeds it at that dose pair. A further combination leaving 65 exceeds HSA but not Bliss. Loewe additivity instead needs equivalent-dose information from suitable individual dose-response curves; this one-point table cannot establish it. Report the model, dose-pair pattern, uncertainty and schedule. Interaction relative to a reference does not identify a biological mechanism, tolerable human exposure or a treatment choice.

A rescue restores a proposed missing function or supply and tests whether a defined effect reverses. Adding a cake mix back after its removal implicates the mixture without identifying flour, sugar or another ingredient; likewise, broad mevalonate add-back does not isolate cholesterol. More specific branch perturbations and appropriate add-backs can narrow the explanation. Partial rescue can reflect incomplete delivery or restoration as well as additional contributors, so it does not prove a second cause. Place the add-back relative to the blocked step: supplying GGPP after an upstream synthesis block is different from inhibiting the transferase that uses GGPP, which the added substrate cannot simply be assumed to bypass. Include restoration-only and matched controls, verify the restored process and distinguish growth, morphology and death. A genetic perturbation also has its own specificity limits.

Attribute each readout to the relevant cells. An ATP-based signal can change through cell number or per-cell metabolism, and slower single-cell mass accumulation does not by itself show death. Direct death measurements and regrowth after washout ask further questions; regrowth concerns surviving cells, not revival of cells already dead. A mixed culture can change composition, and a nonmalignant-cell label alone does not establish a validated healthy-tissue control. Ladan's breast-slice chemotherapy assay was compared with response during preoperative treatment in a defined setting. That assay-specific validation does not validate every postoperative combination, human exposure or clinical decision. An inadequate viable preparation should remain uninterpretable rather than be called resistant.

records.name: CRISPR functional genomics
records.tldr: CRISPR screens test how genetic perturbations change cellular fitness or another measured phenotype in defined models.
records.summary: In pooled CRISPR knockout screens, guide sequences track perturbed populations over time. Relative enrichment or depletion supports a fitness effect under the experimental conditions, including proliferation and survival. Guide delivery and editing efficiency, representation, unintended effects and copy-number-dependent cutting can confound interpretation. Independent perturbations and appropriate follow-up strengthen on-target attribution. Knockout and drug inhibition differ in extent, activity and duration, so a genetic hit does not establish a clinically useful drug.

Shalem et al. 2014, Science: genome-scale CRISPR-Cas9 knockout screening in human cells
Wang et al. 2014, Science: genetic screens in human cells using the CRISPR-Cas9 system
Functional model interpretation: primary evidence
Chronos primary method
Mou et al. 2017: exon skipping after editing
El-Brolosy et al. 2019: scoped genetic compensation

notes: Assay card. Input: enough viable cells to maintain guide representation through delivery, culture and replicate sampling; culture and sequencing consume material. Output: guide counts, log2 fold changes or analysis-specific gene-effect scores, not response probabilities. Retain library, model, screen duration, replicates, quality criteria, analysis version and data release. Non-targeting controls, reference essential genes and concordance across guides assess performance; poor delivery or low representation can leave a screen uninterpretable. Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3972032/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4089965/ CRISPR stands for clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats. A guide RNA directs Cas9 to a DNA sequence; repair after cutting can disrupt gene function. The intended target does not guarantee removal of every functional copy in every cell. Measure the edit and its consequence, rather than equate a barcode with complete knockout.

On-target follow-up is a reading rule: check the edit and functional consequence, reproduce the effect with independent guides or another suitable perturbation, and test whether restoration of the relevant function reverses the phenotype where feasible. Rescue has its own expression and construct controls; failed rescue alone is not proof against the target. This is a causal-comparison framework, not a claim that every published screen performed all these experiments. Responses can include compensation, alternative protein forms or changes in cellular state. Mou reported exon skipping and exon deletions after CRISPR editing, while El-Brolosy studied mutant-mRNA-dependent transcriptional adaptation in zebrafish and mouse models. These bounded findings explain why the resulting RNA, protein and phenotype need checking; they do not establish a universal frequency of compensation. Sources: https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-017-1237-8 ; https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-019-1064-z

Analysis scope. CERES estimates genetic effects while accounting for copy-number cutting effects. Chronos models perturbed population dynamics and was compared with other methods on two pan-cancer datasets and a longitudinal screen. Its reported control separation and bias advantages belong to those comparisons; correction does not make a poor experiment valid. Sources: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5709193/ ; https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-021-02540-7 Cutting several amplified copies can impair growth through DNA damage independently of losing the targeted gene function. In a fictional barcode example, a guide falling from 100 to 20 reads per 10,000 reads has decreased in relative representation; it does not mean that 80 cells died. Proliferation, survival, editing and cutting effects need the separate checks described here.

Some dependencies are shared broadly and others enriched in a particular lineage or genomic context. A gene needed by normal cells may limit therapeutic selectivity. Knockout can remove a protein, whereas a drug may inhibit only one activity partly or temporarily. Guide abundance after perturbation is not RNA expression, and a negative gene-effect score follows the analysis convention rather than guaranteeing drug sensitivity. No screen alone establishes normal-tissue safety. In a fictional amplified-region example, a strong depletion signal becomes small after cutting-toxicity correction; the original rank alone cannot nominate an inhibitor. Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5709193/
records.principle: Track guide representation or a specified phenotype after genetic perturbation, then evaluate controls and context before inferring gene function.
strengths: Systematic interrogation of genetic effects under stated conditions
limitations: Editing and guide performance vary
Copy-number cutting effects and culture context can confound fitness
Genetic effects do not establish drug selectivity or clinical utility

records.name: ctDNA and imaging discordance
records.tldr: A blood DNA result and an imaging result can seem to disagree because they sample different material, regions, times and signals. A mismatch is a question to resolve, not a verdict on either test.
records.summary:
A circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) assay looks for tumour-associated features in a finite sample of cell-free DNA. How much tumour DNA reaches the sampled blood varies between lesions, and recovery, background DNA, the features tracked and the assay's detection limit all shape the call. Imaging measures a defined region through a physical signal. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the breast can report contrast enhancement or the volume of enhancing tissue, which is not a direct count of viable cancer cells. The two tests can therefore differ without either being wrong, and neither automatically replaces the other.

They can also share information. In Magbanua and colleagues' pilot of 84 women having neoadjuvant chemotherapy for early breast cancer, ctDNA concentration was correlated with MRI functional tumour volume at all four time points, with Spearman correlations of 0.42 to 0.49, and patients with detectable ctDNA had a higher median volume. Agreement was partial, and adding ctDNA early in treatment to volume-based prediction of pathological complete response gave only a numerical gain that was not statistically significant. ctDNA positivity after treatment added significantly to volume for predicting distant recurrence and death. A mismatch calls for checking dates, assay limits, the imaged region and the exact finding. It does not by itself show a false test or hidden metastatic disease.

notes: Method card, what is compared: a sampled molecular signal in plasma and a regional physical signal from a named imaging protocol. Their units, dates and thresholds stay separate, and the comparison is only as good as the date alignment of the two acquisitions.

Table, blood side: input is a blood draw and the plasma and recovered DNA analysed, and testing consumes an aliquot. Output is a qualifying call plus a defined concentration or fraction, read with the assay's detection and quantitation rules. Failure modes are low shedding, finite input, poor recovery and background or blood-cell variants.

Table, imaging side: input is the imaged region and a protocol, and contrast or tracer use depends on the modality. Output is size, volume, uptake or a qualitative finding read against protocol-specific response criteria. Failure modes are artefacts, non-tumour contributions to the signal and technique that differs between visits.

Table, what each cannot tell: blood alone cannot locate a lesion or give a cell count. Imaging alone cannot count viable tumour cells, and enhancement can have more than one tissue cause. Neither agreement nor disagreement shows that a treatment change would help, which is a clinical-utility question.

Evidence read: Magbanua's pilot (84 patients, MTM/mL against MRI functional tumour volume) found correlation at T0 to T3 with rho 0.49, 0.42, 0.42 and 0.43, and its authors call the findings preliminary in a limited cohort needing larger validation. It supports partial agreement and does not set a rule for redirecting treatment.

Interpretation rule, from finite sampling: a plasma aliquot can hold no tumour molecule when the true share is small, so no qualifying ctDNA signal alongside an abnormal MRI region does not show the region is only scar. The converse holds too: a clear image does not exclude tumour DNA in blood. Each result answers only its own question.

Source attribution comes first: a positive plasma variant may come from a blood-cell clone rather than a tumour. In Razavi's paired sequencing, 53.2% of cell-free DNA mutations in 124 people with metastatic cancer and 81.6% in 47 people without cancer had features of clonal haematopoiesis, so a discordant positive needs origin checks before it is read as occult disease.

Half-life, scoped: Diehl and colleagues estimated a ctDNA half-life after surgery of 114 minutes by evaluating one subject whose plasma was sampled at several early times after complete resection in a study of 162 plasma samples from 18 subjects with colorectal cancer (Diehl 2008). That is a single-subject estimate of post-resection clearance in colorectal cancer, not a universal cfDNA half-life, a breast-cancer figure or a blood-draw schedule. DNA release and clearance can change sooner than visible tissue structure, which is a reason to align the dates of the blood and imaging acquisitions.

Use the blood collection date and imaging acquisition date to compare biology, then keep the reporting dates as a separate measure of when the information became available. Imaging does not remove a tissue aliquot for molecular analysis; contrast or tracer use belongs to the specific protocol. Agreement can reflect shared dependence on disease burden and is not two independent proofs of the same mechanism. Combining measurements into a decision rule needs validation of the combination and its intended outcome.

In a fictional early-breast-cancer example, a negative plasma result is not an examination of the breast tumour bed or regional nodes. It cannot by itself establish pathological complete response or validate skipping surgery. Using a result to remove a treatment needs evidence for that decision strategy and its clinical outcomes, beyond showing that an assay can detect a signal. This is an interpretation limit, not a claim that no omission study exists.

The two-window comparison is about scope. A finite plasma aliquot contains extracellular DNA, of which tumour-derived fragments may be one part; breast MRI observes regional, sequence-dependent features rather than individual cancer cells. Contrast enhancement reflects vascular and contrast-delivery behaviour as well as the acquisition protocol; it is not a one-to-one viable-cell count. In the 84-person I-SPY2 MRI pilot, functional tumour volume summed voxels meeting 70% enhancement about two and a half minutes after contrast, inside a manually drawn box around the lesion. A camera-and-stream analogy illustrates those two sampled views without promising that every tumour sheds DNA. Keep the imaging method visible: mammography uses X-rays, ultrasound uses sound, and PET/CT combines tracer-distribution images with anatomical CT images. A formal response category needs its framework, comparison timepoint and findings outside a selected lesion measurement. None of these measurements is an interchangeable all-body tumour-cell number.

Four patterns illustrate the reading boundary. A smaller lesion and lower detected blood signal mean that both recorded measures fell in their own units, not that pCR or eradication of distant disease is proved. A residual scan finding with undetected blood leaves viability, treatment effects and other causes unresolved. Detected blood with no suspicious finding in the scanned region does not establish the signal's location, full extent or best intervention. If neither shows qualifying evidence, neither has proved zero microscopic disease or justified omitting indicated treatment. These are interpretation examples, not an action algorithm; disagreement alone does not establish pseudoprogression.

In a fictional course, a breast lesion becomes less enhancing, blood changes from detected to not detected, and surgery later finds residual invasive cancer. There is no contradiction: imaging features, a finite molecular sample and removed tissue answer different questions. Only the specified tissue assessment establishes the residual disease in this example. A smaller scan finding and undetected blood can therefore be favourable observations without confirming pCR. Conversely, a later positive blood result with clear regional breast imaging calls for review of sample qualification, origin, dates and clinical context; it is not itself a diagnosis of distant metastasis.

Magbanua and colleagues' 2025 analysis evaluated 723 high-risk I-SPY2 patients across hormone receptor-positive/HER2-negative, triple-negative and HER2-positive subtypes. Combining ctDNA with residual cancer burden refined prognostic groups, but analyses within those groups used smaller subsets, some too small for multivariable adjustment. The authors also found retained patient-specific assay variants in sampled resistant tumours from patients whose post-treatment plasma was negative. These results support studying risk information and shedding; they do not turn negative presurgical blood into tissue pCR or demonstrate that a blood-guided omission strategy improves outcomes.

records.name: Curesponse
records.tldr: Israeli company whose cResponse test keeps a patient's tumour fragment alive, with its vessels and immune cells, to test which treatments it responds to.
records.summary: Curesponse, based in Rehovot, Israel, and founded in 2018, is the company whose cResponse test keeps a fragment of a patient's tumour alive, with its blood vessels and immune cells intact, to test which treatments it responds to. The test combines ex vivo tumour-fragment culture with rapid genomics and is distributed in the United Kingdom through EDX Medical. Bar and colleagues' 2026 postmarket surveillance report analysed 278 of 312 tested patients, with clinical-response information from 45 survey respondents. Its methods describe exclusions from a treatment-choice analysis, so this proportion is not by itself a culture-establishment success rate. Reported response agreement and changed physician decisions do not establish improved patient outcomes from using the test. OnCo links it to functional ex vivo drug testing and organoid-guided therapy at scale, to the bottleneck of preclinical models that do not predict people, and to ideas on testing drugs on freshly cut slices of the patient's own tumour. Outcome evidence is specific to the assay and intended use; a randomised result for another functional test does not establish benefit from choosing treatment with cResponse. The functional testing page carries the evidence.

records.name: Data leakage in model evaluation
records.tldr: Leakage is when information from the test data reaches the model during training, through a scaler fitted on all samples, a patient split across folds or a benchmark that appeared in the pretraining set, making the model look better than it is.
records.summary: In statistics and machine learning, leakage is the use of information during training that would not be available at prediction time, which produces overly optimistic performance estimates (Wikipedia). Common cancer-data forms are normalising or selecting genes on the full cohort before splitting, duplicated patients across TCGA and cBioPortal studies, and benchmark contamination, where a foundation model's pretraining corpus contained the public test set (TCGA slides or profiles), so that its downstream score is partly recall.

records.name: Denominators and conditional probability
records.tldr: A percentage answers a question about a particular group. Name that group before interpreting the number, and keep unknown outcomes separate from measured non-response.
records.summary: A proportion identifies an outcome within a defined group. The denominator might be everyone enrolled, everyone treated, people with an evaluable scan, or only people with a recurrence; those answer different questions. Conditional probability makes the specified group explicit and is not a statement of causation. Repeated measurements do not create new independent people. Unknown outcomes and incomplete follow-up require explicit handling rather than being silently treated as measured non-response.

links.label: Hernan and Robins: Causal Inference: What If
CONSORT 2025: explanation and elaboration
FDA: oncology clinical-trial endpoints (2018)
OncoGuide: denominators-and-conditional-probability (pinned teaching source)

notes: “Half had a response” is incomplete until the counted group is named. The numerator counts observations meeting the event rule; the denominator identifies the relevant group or observation amount. Conditional probability P(A | B) means the probability of A among those satisfying B, with P(A | B) = P(A and B)/P(B) when P(B) is positive. It is undefined if that conditioning probability is zero. “Given” does not mean “caused by”, and the probability of a positive test among people with disease differs from the probability of disease among people with a positive test. People, lesions, blood draws and wells supply different denominators. Events per person-time are a rate, not a simple probability; repeated samples do not become independent patients. A group defined by treatment response may also be selected by underlying biology, so a conditional frequency does not show that the treatment caused the difference. A changed proportion needs its reference proportion attached, because percentages and percentage points answer different questions.

A fictional study enrols twenty people, six never receive the product, fourteen are treated, ten have evaluable scans and five meet the response rule. The observed response proportions are 5/20 = 25% among enrolled people, 5/14, about 35.7%, among treated people, and 5/10 = 50% among those with evaluable scans. The scan-evaluable group is nested within the treated group, which is nested within enrolment. Five other evaluable scans did not meet the response rule; four treated people lack evaluable scans and six were untreated, with no response outcomes supplied for those groups. Calling them confirmed nonresponders would add an assumption. A protocol may classify missing assessments as nonresponse, but that rule and its sensitivity analyses should be reported explicitly.

In a separate complete fictional cohort of 100 people, twenty recur and five of those have brain involvement. Brain involvement is 5/20 = 25% among those with recurrence and 5/100 = 5% in the original cohort. Neither is a personal forecast. In another example with forty enrolled, thirty treated, twenty evaluable and eight responses, 8/20 = 40% describes the evaluable group, whereas 8/40 = 20% describes observed responders among everyone enrolled without establishing the other outcomes. Incomplete follow-up also means recorded events divided by enrolment may not estimate risk at a chosen time; survival or competing-risk methods address defined questions under their assumptions. Safety and efficacy tables can use different analysis sets, and biomarker subgroups or later landmarks change who contributes. Multiple reports from the same participants add no independent people. Exclusion because progression prevented assessment can itself affect interpretation.

records.name: Endpoint
records.tldr: An endpoint specifies an outcome and how and when it is assessed. A study's statistical plan determines what counts as meeting its primary endpoint.
records.summary: A trial defines primary, secondary and exploratory outcomes and how they are measured and analysed. The primary question informs design, sample size and testing; having a secondary endpoint does not by itself establish whether it was adequately powered or met a prespecified testing rule. Overall survival concerns death from any cause, while response, progression, symptoms and quality of life answer different questions. A composite endpoint combines specified events, so its definition and starting time matter. FDA's December 2018 nonbinding oncology-endpoint guidance distinguishes direct clinical benefit and context-dependent surrogate evidence; use in an approval does not make an endpoint interchangeable with survival in every setting.

links.label: Wikipedia
ICH E9(R1): estimands, intercurrent events and sensitivity analysis (May 2021)
FDA: oncology clinical endpoints, nonbinding guidance (December 2018)

notes: A study question card keeps the population and setting, prior treatment and exclusions, complete intervention and comparator, endpoint definition and assessment, starting clock and horizon together. The intervention may be a sequence of medicines, procedures and surgery. Read the protocol and analysis plan for treatment stopping, switching and missing outcomes. A percentage without these details may answer a different question from the proposed action.

Consider a fictional trial in operable cancer with one random assignment to study drug plus common chemotherapy, surgery and study drug afterwards, or placebo on the same sequence. Comparing the whole assigned strategies does not isolate starting the drug only after surgery, because there is no second postoperative assignment. From the common randomisation origin, a recurrence in someone still alive and a death without earlier recurrence both count in a recurrence-or-death composite; only the death counts in overall survival. An improvement in a composite need not mean that every component improved. This is a reasoning example, with no dosing schedule or effect size.

For another fictional comparison, 95% alive three years after surgery and 90% free of recurrence or death three years after randomisation cannot be ranked as if they measured one outcome. The events and starting clocks differ; someone alive with recurrence contributes differently. An event-free percentage is not a permanent cure rate. State the eligible population, both complete strategies, event definition and origin before interpreting a benefit.

records.name: Ex vivo tumour fragments and slices
records.tldr: Living tumour pieces can retain local cells and architecture for a defined experiment outside the body, while losing circulating supply and recruitment.
records.summary: Fragment and slice preparations retain selected native tissue relationships rather than expanding a selected culture. Composition and function change with sampling, cutting, diffusion, medium and time. A retained vessel does not demonstrate perfusion, and visible immune cells do not establish the required interaction. Ladan's breast-slice assay and Salmon's human lung-slice migration experiments support different questions; neither validates every fragment test or treatment decision.

links.label: Ladan et al. 2023 primary slice assay
Salmon et al. 2012 primary lung-tissue interaction
Hafner et al. 2016: readout interpretation, not fragment validation
FDA: statistical guidance for diagnostic test studies (March 2007)

notes: Preparation and assay card. Input: suitable viable tissue with donor/site/time, collection and transport conditions, dimensions and culture window. Cutting, quality checks and endpoints consume finite material and limit available conditions. Compare baseline quality and untreated or carrier controls with defined exposures. Attribute counts, stain fractions, movement or metabolic signal to the relevant cells, with units, time and denominator. Thresholds are method-specific rather than a universal fragment score. Fragment names the preparation; a drug screen names an experiment it may support. Different pieces from one tumour can contain different populations, so matched treatments still need composition checks.

Primary preparation example. Ladan used 300 micrometre slices and three-day exposure in a defined anthracycline-based assay, measuring morphology, proliferation and apoptosis. Diffusion into slices differs from vascular delivery; host metabolic activation, clearance, organ toxicity and new immune recruitment were not recreated. Preparation injury, poor viability, uneven diffusion, changing populations and non-tumour signal can invalidate interpretation. A failed culture is not evidence of clinical resistance. Contamination is another reason for assay failure; short-term response does not establish durable elimination, systemic safety or benefit.

Endpoint and validation example. Ladan reported 23 usable assays among 30 tumour-containing biopsies; three of the 23 did not proceed to the clinical treatment comparison, leaving 20 evaluable patients and 15 concordant MRI comparisons. The agreement compared sensitive, intermediate and resistant categories after four courses of anthracycline-containing chemotherapy; it is not a binary drug-killing rate. The study did not observe an ex vivo resistant group, limiting assessment of resistance detection. Those denominators, assay version and preoperative setting cannot validate another postoperative choice. Salmon measured matrix-associated T-cell location and movement in viable lung-tumour slices, not treatment-selection benefit.

Fictional reading exercise. Two fragments with different starting malignant-cell fractions both lose total metabolic signal. Equal tumour killing has not been shown. Verify composition and an attributed death endpoint against controls. Retained neighbours can be useful for an immune question only when their viability and relevant function are demonstrated.

Ladan's real study began with 41 consenting people: three did not undergo biopsy and eight biopsies lacked tumour cells, leaving 30 adequate tumour biopsies. Six assays failed the prespecified baseline-apoptosis criterion and one was lost to infection. Of 23 usable results, three people did not receive the chemotherapy, leaving 20 clinical comparisons. The main-text counts are used here; Table 2's footnote instead mentions two people not receiving chemotherapy. The reported interval for 15/20 agreement was 53 to 89 percent, and the pilot's prespecified target was at least 55 percent. Reaching that target supports further investigation, not a demonstration that using the assay to choose care improves outcomes.

The reported breast-study totals imply two sensitive dish calls with sensitive MRI, three sensitive dish calls with intermediate MRI, two intermediate dish calls with sensitive MRI and thirteen intermediate calls matching MRI. Thus 15/20 agree, including thirteen matches in the common intermediate category. Two of four MRI-sensitive tumours were called sensitive in the dish (50 percent), and two of five sensitive dish calls matched MRI sensitivity (40 percent). These are stated comparisons with an imperfect MRI outcome, not validated sensitivity or positive predictive value against known truth. FDA's March 2007 diagnostic-test guidance distinguishes agreement from accuracy when the comparator is not a reference standard. The study's sensitive category required more than 50 percent size reduction after four chemotherapy courses; it is not simply the standard RECIST partial-response category. Usable coverage is 23/30, about 77 percent; a matching clinical comparison was available for 15/30, or 50 percent, including failures and the untreated people in that denominator. Neither ratio measures postoperative benefit.
records.principle: Maintain viable tissue pieces for a defined comparison while measuring retained populations, quality and an attributed response.

records.name: External validation
records.tldr: External evaluation estimates model performance on data not used to develop or tune it. The patients, setting and methods determine which transportability question it addresses; it does not by itself establish useful clinical decisions.
records.summary: External evaluation applies an existing model to data outside its development and compares predictions with observed outcomes. The TRIPOD-Cluster explanation includes later-period data collected by the same investigators as well as data from another hospital, country or care setting. A different platform is not a universal requirement. Apparent performance uses the development data and can be optimistic. Internal validation with resampling can estimate optimism and performance for new people from the same source population; it is evidence about a different question, rather than no result. External evaluation quantifies performance and its uncertainty instead of conferring a universal pass or fail. Keep the locked method, population, outcome, follow-up and differences from development visible.

links.label: Wikipedia
Debray et al.: TRIPOD-Cluster explanation, development and evaluation (2023)
Michiels et al.: repeated-split reanalysis of seven microarray prognosis studies (2005)

notes: Follow the people behind a performance plot: eligibility, selection, care, sample quality, failures and missing outcomes. Identify every variable-selection, preprocessing and threshold choice and whether outcomes were known when those choices were made. Good performance on ideal specimens or the development patients may not describe practice. External evaluation uses data outside development, which can differ in hospital, calendar period, handling or care. The data and evaluation need to be independent of the tuning decisions; a new company logo supplies no such guarantee.

Two fictional slides illustrate the boundary. Slide A uses Hospital A patients and their known outcomes to select variables and a threshold, then reports performance on those same A patients. That is apparent performance; repeating the computation can check reproducibility without providing a new independent population test. Slide B fixes preprocessing, variables and threshold using A before applying the locked method to separate Hospital B patients. It reports B performance and the failed-test denominator, with no B outcomes fed back into tuning. This supports evaluation outside development, while suitable population, uncertainty, calibration and usefulness of clinical decisions remain separate questions. The patient icons are schematic and neither slide supplies a measured performance value.

Michiels and colleagues reanalysed the seven largest published microarray cancer-prognosis studies in their 2005 report using multiple random training and evaluation sets. They found unstable gene signatures and overoptimistic published estimates; five of the seven did not classify patients better than chance. That historical result supports retaining the entire selection and evaluation process, not a conclusion that every molecular model fails or that this one analysis establishes a universal validation method.

A model evaluated at a second hospital may still address advanced treated disease rather than the proposed postoperative use. Discrimination asks whether outcomes are ranked usefully; calibration asks whether stated probabilities agree with observed frequencies in comparable groups. Good ranking can coexist with inflated risk estimates, and good prognostic probabilities do not establish benefit from a treatment printed beside them. There is no single performance cutoff that makes every decision appropriate. If unchanged Hospital A samples are rerun, request an evaluation set held out from every tuning choice, a locked method, target population and outcome, all failure denominators and uncertainty. Internal resampling and independent external evaluation answer different performance questions; neither name alone is a clinical-use verdict.

records.name: Foundation model
records.tldr: A foundation model learns reusable representations from broad data and can be adapted to different tasks. Its performance needs evaluation for each task and setting.
records.summary: A foundation model learns reusable representations during pretraining and can be adapted to different tasks. Geneformer was pretrained on about 30 million single-cell transcriptomes and scGPT on over 33 million cells, then adapted to downstream tasks (Theodoris and colleagues, 2023; Cui and colleagues, 2024). Pretraining and task-specific fitting are different stages, and zero-shot use (no further training), fine-tuning and a small predictor fitted on frozen features are different evaluation settings that should not be compared as if they used the same information. A zero-shot evaluation of Geneformer and scGPT found that in some cases they were outperformed by simpler methods; one evaluation dataset partly overlapped Geneformer's pretraining data and two were included in scGPT's, so overlap between pretraining and test data has to be checked, including whether the same participants or donors sit on both sides (the TRIPOD+AI reporting guidance asks that evaluation data share no participants with the data used to train, tune or select a model; Kedzierska and colleagues, 2025). A 2025 benchmark found that none of five single-cell foundation models and two other deep-learning models beat deliberately simple baselines at predicting transcriptome changes after single or double gene perturbations (Ahlmann-Eltze and colleagues, 2025). An embedding is a computed representation, not a measured function, and a published result belongs to its model version, task, data and adaptation method. Foundation model, generative model and virtual cell are overlapping but different ideas: an AI virtual cell is described as a multi-scale, multi-modal large neural network model (Bunne and colleagues, 2024, a perspective rather than a validation), and none of the labels shows that simulated interventions predict tumour killing or improve care. Failure modes worth recording are population or assay mismatch, leakage, technical shortcuts, unavailable input features and poor calibration.

Input and cost: the data type, preparation and normalisation used; running a model uses computing resources and no new tissue, but the original assays that produced the data consumed specimens. Output and units: embedding coordinates, labels or predicted molecular values, with the original units and transforms kept. Controls and thresholds: baselines that use the same information, independent evaluation, and a decision rule set before testing; there is no general passing size or score. Failure modes: population or assay mismatch, leakage, technical shortcuts, unavailable features and poor calibration. Validation tier: evidence for the stated task only, with no implied clinical authorisation or benefit.

records.name: Functional (ex vivo) drug testing
records.tldr: Functional drug testing measures a defined response to medicines in collected living material under laboratory conditions.
records.summary: Functional drug testing exposes a defined living preparation to medicines and measures a specified response. Preparations may use dissociated cells, expanded organoids or short-term tissue cultures. Feasibility, outcome agreement and benefit from using a result to choose care are separate questions and must be tied to the actual assay version, cancer, treatment and setting.

Breast-slice assay version and handling
Promega CellTiter-Glo: ATP readout and cellular-content limitations
Restivo et al. 2022: protocol-specific recovery from slow-frozen tumour tissue
Ooft et al.: SENSOR organoid-guided treatment study (2021)

notes: Specimen and assay card. Record donor/site/time, living preparation, transport and processing, initial composition, culture history, assay version, concentrations, exposure duration, replicates and control range. Fixed tissue cannot supply living cells; whether previously frozen material can supply the required viable preparation must be demonstrated for that protocol. Input suitability and recovery must be demonstrated for the method. Testing and endpoint processing use finite material. Output needs units, denominator, normalisation and uncertainty; acceptance criteria must be defined for the actual method. Name whether the preparation is dissociated cells, a fresh fragment or an expanded organoid. Mixed samples include normal neighbours, and expansion can change the represented populations.

Handling evidence is method-specific. Ladan and colleagues collected breast tissue in their specified medium, cut 300 micrometre slices and assessed morphology, proliferation and apoptosis after three-day exposure. This is not a general transport or storage protocol for all screens. Growth-rate methods show why baseline counts and control division affect interpretation. Retain failures and exclusions; failed preparation is not clinical resistance. Sources: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10542784/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4887336/ Medium, drug access and exposure duration can change the result. Mechanism-relevant controls test whether the claimed interaction can occur; absent required cells or unrealistic exposures can make an experiment uninformative even when a numerical response is available. A laboratory concentration is not a safe human dose.

Fictional example. A well has half the metabolic signal but the same identified viable tumour-cell endpoint count as control. This establishes a changed proxy, not half the cells killed; endpoint equality also does not reconstruct every division and death. Separate death, target engagement, safe human dosing and clinical benefit remain questions. This is an arithmetic and interpretation exercise, not observed patient data. Possible readouts include cell number, metabolism, mass, growth and death. Adenosine triphosphate (ATP) is a cellular energy molecule measured by some luminescence assays. Promega's primary assay guidance states that cellular ATP content varies with cell type and physiology and can alter the relation between cell number and light output. A lower ATP signal can therefore reflect fewer cells or a per-cell change, rather than a counted death fraction. Source: https://www.promega.com/-/media/files/resources/protocols/technical-bulletins/0/celltiter-glo-luminescent-cell-viability-assay-protocol.pdf

Restivo and colleagues generated organoids from matched fresh and slow-frozen colorectal tumour tissue from two patients with stage IV disease. Their specified slow-freezing protocol used a cryoprotectant to preserve living material, and the frozen-derived cultures took longer to form than the fresh-derived cultures. This is evidence of recovery under that protocol, not equivalence of all fresh, snap-frozen and viable-cryopreserved samples or a guaranteed turnaround. The handling history, recovery, malignant identity and assay quality need checking for the intended experiment. Preserved molecular material alone does not establish a recoverable living model. Source: https://doi.org/10.1038/s42003-022-04025-0

Read a model study as a sequence of explicitly defined groups: people or specimens offered or submitted, preparations yielding a usable model, results compared with a clinical outcome, and results agreeing under the stated rule. Eligibility exclusions, absent tumour, laboratory failures, missing outcomes and people not receiving the treatment belong to different steps. State whether the unit is a person, specimen or treatment comparison; one person can contribute more than one. A percentage among compared cases cannot describe everyone originally offered testing, and an analysis exclusion is not automatically a failed culture. Keep the drug, cancer, treatment history, outcome, clock and assay version attached rather than ranking different studies as competing accuracy scores.

The prospective single-arm SENSOR study enrolled 61 people with metastatic colorectal cancer: 54 were eligible, 31 organoids were generated, 25 cultures were screened against eight drugs and nineteen showed a substantial laboratory response. Six people received an organoid-selected treatment, three vistusertib and three capivasertib, with no objective clinical responses. That observation concerns this panel and selected population; it neither establishes benefit from using the assay nor proves that every organoid method is ineffective. Guillen and colleagues' breast-model report describes a complete response in one person with metastatic triple-negative disease after a model-nominated treatment. That case demonstrates feasibility, without a comparison estimating how often the strategy helps.

Randomised outcome evidence must be assessed for the named assay and use rather than declared absent for all functional testing in solid tumours. Ranjan and colleagues reported a 2023 trial of ChemoID selection versus physician choice from the same chemotherapy list in 78 people with recurrent glioblastoma under the 2016 WHO definition. Enrolment stopped after a prespecified efficacy analysis; the intention-to-treat report gave median overall survival of twelve versus 7.5 months. Participants could provide viable tumour through surgery or biopsy, so the findings do not include every patient with recurrent glioblastoma. Cordgenics supported the assay resources, and two authors declared licensed intellectual-property interests. This is evidence for the studied strategy and population, without validating another assay, organoid system, postoperative breast decision or universal treatment rule.
records.principle: Compare defined exposures with matched controls in a characterised viable preparation; attribute the endpoint to the relevant population.
strengths: Tests a drug-response hypothesis directly in a defined preparation
Can compare several exposures when material permits
limitations: Preparation, viability, sampling and turnaround affect feasibility
Missing components can leave a drug mechanism untested
Outcome association alone does not establish clinical utility

records.name: Comparing tumour-model preparations
records.tldr: Choose a preparation by the biology and time the question requires, then verify its actual components and endpoint.
records.summary: Conventional xenografts, epithelial organoids and short-term fragments make different trade-offs. Xenografts add a living host with mouse support and exposure. Organoids expand selected populations in supplied culture conditions. Fragments can retain local neighbours briefly without perfused circulation. This comparison describes preparations and decision windows; the existing model-context framework owns the broader question of intended-use validation.

notes: A conventional xenograft implants viable tumour material into a host; an epithelial organoid grows selected cells in supplied matrix and medium; a fragment or slice retains a cut piece of local tissue. Ladan used 300 micrometre (0.3 millimetre) breast slices. None supplies complete human drug metabolism, healthy-organ toxicity or recruitment of new immune cells from human circulation, and every preparation can fail. Fixed archival tissue cannot supply the living input. Whether frozen material is usable must be shown for the particular protocol; Ladan's assay used fresh tissue.

Throughput and repetition depend on how material can be expanded. A xenograft can be passaged into further mice, but each drug comparison needs suitable animals and controls. An established organoid line can be expanded and passaged to compare a drug panel; Sachs reported retention of many source features during extended passaging, not unlimited fidelity. A cut piece has a finite culture window and a limited number of matched conditions; it cannot simply be expanded while retaining the same original neighbourhood. Ladan's group described viability for up to a week. These are practical preparation contrasts, not a universal numerical throughput ranking or an assumption that every organoid survives freezing. Sources: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2017.11.010 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10542784/

The useful trade-off is preserved biology against time and repeatability. A characterised PDX supports growth under whole-animal dosing, usually on a months-long establishment clock. Expanded organoids support repeated direct tumour-cell experiments and panels, often over weeks; conventional epithelial cultures usually lack immune cells, while Neal's specialised method retained them. A short-term fragment may preserve resident neighbours for a local-interaction question over days, but their function must be demonstrated. No preparation is universally more predictive because it is more complex. Sources: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2018.11.021 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4167608/

The clocks and take rates below belong to different studies. Hidalgo's review described four to eight months to a study-ready PDX. Izumchenko reported 578/1,163 establishment and mean 16 weeks from engraftment to drug exposure, with tumour-type variation: 85 percent in colorectal specimens and 30 percent in breast specimens in that series. Cartry reported a 61.5 percent core-biopsy take rate and six-week median, range four to ten weeks, to a 25-drug colorectal organoid panel. Boileve reported 54/87 establishment (62 percent) and mean 6.8 weeks to a pancreatic chemogram. Ladan used three-day exposures and stated that results can be known in seven to fourteen days; this is a planned window, not an observed turnaround distribution. There were 23/30 usable tests from tumour-containing biopsies. The PDX paper reports 49 percent for 578/1,163; direct count arithmetic is approximately 49.7 percent.

Ladan's breast-slice pilot found 15/20 category matches (75 percent; reported confidence interval 53 to 89 percent), against a pre-set target of at least 55 percent, between the ex vivo anthracycline assay and MRI response after four courses of anthracycline-containing treatment. Both systems used sensitive, intermediate and resistant categories, and neither observed a resistant tumour. Of five disagreements, three were ex vivo sensitive with intermediate MRI response and two the reverse. Among the 23 successful laboratory tests, six were sensitive and 17 intermediate; among the 20 MRI comparisons, four were sensitive and 16 intermediate. This leaves resistance detection untested rather than established. Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10542784/

Other agreement measures answer different questions. Vlachogiannis reported 88 percent positive and 100 percent negative predictive values in 21 drug-response comparisons in heavily pretreated gastrointestinal cancers. Boileve reported 83.3 percent sensitivity and 92.9 percent specificity in 34 evaluable pretreated pancreatic patients. Izumchenko compared 129 treatments across 92 patients: 112/129 agreement grouped stable disease with partial and complete responses, while exact-category agreement was 91/129. These endpoints and selected denominators cannot be ranked as head-to-head accuracy or taken as proof that model-guided care improves survival.

Voabil's primary abstract reports that immune-cell reactivation after ex vivo PD-1 blockade in patient-derived tumour fragments predicted clinical response in that study, with perturbation analyses identifying tumour-resident T cells as a key component. This supports a scoped fragment/immune-interaction example, not evidence that choosing treatment from a fragment test improves outcomes. A near-term decision may rule out establishing a new conventional PDX, but does not guarantee a usable fragment; immune presence, movement, recognition and killing remain distinct measurements. Source: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41591-021-01398-3

Dijkstra's colorectal and lung organoid study used master and working biobanks, cryopreserved cultures and experiments below passage 30. That demonstrates a specified bank-and-recovery workflow for those established organoid cultures. It does not show that every organoid line or fresh tumour fragment can be frozen, recovered and retested with unchanged properties. Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6558289/

In a wholly fictional development project, D0 supplies one verified malignant preparation. Drug A asks about a direct repair perturbation: a tumour-only organoid supplies a viable-cell count after 48 hours, with division and death measured separately. The invented exposure series is 0.1, 0.3 and 1 micromoles per litre with three wells per condition and vehicle, positive and mechanism controls. Antibody B instead needs compatible tumour and immune populations over a stipulated seven days, with tumour-only, immune-only, matched antibody or carrier, and recognition controls. B's concentration and schedule are missing. The conventional graft's mouse exposure, schedule, assessment day and controls are also missing, so it remains an incomplete proposal. These conditions are not doses established as safe or achievable in people.

A separate fictional three-week decision exercise names real drugs but invents every result. A tumour-only organoid can test a direct olaparib response using an attributed living-cell count after five days; it cannot supply the T cells needed for the pembrolizumab question. Fresh fragments retaining functional resident T cells or a characterised compatible co-culture can address a two-day activation question, with attributed tumour-cell death and recognition controls still needed. A conventional graft cannot restore an intact human immune system and its establishment may miss the deadline. Predicting RNA after BRCA1 loss is a computational hypothesis, not a performed drug exposure. Confirm the actual assay clock: a colorectal six-week median does not forecast the timing for this fictional breast specimen. No choice supplies complete human metabolism, healthy-organ toxicity or every original tumour population.

records.name: Ex vivo drug sensitivity screening in blood cancers (EXALT)
records.tldr: Ex vivo drug screening measures responses in collected blood-cancer cells to support research and defined clinical studies; a ranked result requires clinical interpretation.
records.summary: Ex vivo blood-cancer screening measures a specified response in collected malignant and comparator populations. Results depend on the specimen, preparation, treatment exposure and assay. The EXALT study is one clinical investigation of a defined selection approach; a screen result alone does not establish a safe treatment, and failed or uninterpretable experiments are not clinical resistance findings. Generalisation to another cancer, assay or decision strategy requires separate evidence.

links.label: Cancer Discovery 2022: Functional precision medicine provides clinical benefit in advanced aggressive hematologic cancers and identifies exceptional responders (EXALT)
Growth-rate readout interpretation in cell lines: Hafner et al. 2016

notes: Assay-report axes. Name the malignant population and comparator cells, live input and consumption, drug concentration and exposure, readout and denominator, control range, failures and assay version. A mixed malignant/normal ratio can change through either population; it is not by itself a counted malignant-cell death fraction. Negative or failed experiments do not automatically nominate another clinical treatment. These are reading rules, not changes to the EXALT trial result. Source for growth/readout boundary: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4887336/

The prospective EXALT study tested an image-based single-cell selection approach in 143 people with advanced aggressive blood cancers. Fifty-six were treated according to the assay; 30 of those 56 (54 percent) had progression-free survival at least 1.3 times that on their own previous therapy. The comparator was each person's prior therapy in a single-arm study, not randomised standard care. This result does not show that all tested patients benefited or validate another assay or disease setting. Source: https://doi.org/10.1158/2159-8290.CD-21-0538

EXALT used viable material from blood, bone marrow or lymph nodes. These are method- and disease-specific inputs, not evidence that every blood cancer is easy to sample or that its test transfers to a solid-tumour preparation. The 143 enrolled and tested people, 56 receiving assay-guided therapy and 30 meeting the PFS-ratio endpoint remain distinct groups. The comparator for that endpoint was each person's previous therapy; another twenty people formed a physician-choice observational cohort, without random allocation.
records.principle: A specified viability or imaging assay measures response in identified malignant and comparator cells after defined exposures.
strengths: Tests drug response in collected patient cells under defined laboratory conditions
limitations: Results depend on specimen quality, composition, assay and disease setting
A dish does not reproduce whole-body exposure or complete immunity
Clinical validity and benefit from a selection strategy require distinct evidence

records.name: Immune-tumour co-culture models
records.tldr: Co-culture places tumour and immune populations together so researchers can measure their interactions with identified cells and appropriate controls.
records.summary: Co-culture studies interactions among defined populations. Dijkstra and colleagues combined autologous blood lymphocytes with tumour organoids from mismatch repair-deficient colorectal cancer and from non-small-cell lung cancer, with enrichment and later killing measurements as separate stages. Neal and colleagues retained native immune components using a specialised air-liquid-interface organoid method. Presence, activation, tumour recognition and killing require different observations; neither model label establishes universal patient prediction.
