notes: Controls and compartments. Compare tumour-only, neighbour-only and mixed cultures, with matched vehicle or exposure controls. Direct contact allows contact and exchanged molecules; a selected permeable support can separate cells while allowing exchange, but passage depends on membrane and cells. Previously collected cell-free conditioned medium tests transferred secreted material, not ongoing reciprocal interaction. These comparisons isolate different questions rather than rank culture formats. Source for separated support design: https://www.corning.com/worldwide/en/products/life-sciences/products/permeable-supports/transwell-guidelines.html Autologous populations come from the same person; allogeneic populations come from different people. Human leukocyte antigen (HLA) differences can themselves provoke T-cell recognition in an allogeneic experiment. Macdonald's primary structural study showed HLA- and peptide-dependent human T-cell alloreactivity; it did not validate a tumour-response test. Even autologous cells may lack relevant tumour-reactive cells or change during culture. Source: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.immuni.2009.09.025

Dijkstra primary study: a two-week enrichment stage preceded a separate three-day organoid-killing assessment. Matched healthy organoids and HLA-blocking comparisons tested specificity; reactions to xenogeneic Geltrex matrix were also investigated. A marker or cytokine signal alone did not substitute for the identified live-cell/death readout. The studied donors and protocol define the scope: the colorectal samples were mismatch repair-deficient, and the defined T-cell response occurred in four of eight patients with MHC class I-positive organoids in the colorectal comparison. No response was observed in the tested MHC class I-deficient lines. These timings are not universal culture windows. Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6558289/ Jenkins also described organotypic spheroids retaining autologous immune and stromal components. Added blood lymphocytes and retained tumour neighbours are different preparations; measure retention and function over the actual window rather than assign immune capability exclusively to one format. Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5809290/

Assay card. Retain source donor/site/time for each viable population, autologous or allogeneic relationship, starting ratio, medium, persistence and readout time. Isolation, expansion and assays consume finite material. Report identified live target counts, a death fraction with denominator, or cytokine concentration with units. Check viability, missing reactive cells, incompatible medium, changing ratios, matrix/allogeneic responses and bulk-signal attribution. Quality thresholds are method-specific; replicates from one donor do not establish population validation.

In a fictional mixed culture, a metabolic signal falls by half, but identified viable tumour-cell counts are unchanged and viable immune-cell counts fall. The bulk decline could come from the immune compartment and does not show 50 percent tumour killing. Population-specific survival and death measurements are needed; activation, recognition and killing remain distinct endpoints.
records.principle: Define added or retained populations and interaction compartments, then measure population-specific responses with appropriate controls.
strengths: Tests an immune-tumour interaction under controlled, defined conditions
Can enrich tumour-reactive T cells in a studied protocol
Can model aspects of checkpoint blockade in specialised systems
limitations: Cell proportions and phenotype can change during culture
Autologous origin alone does not establish tumour specificity
Body-level exposure, recruitment and clinical utility remain outside the culture alone

records.name: In vitro and in vivo
records.tldr: Experimental settings describe where and how a test occurs: laboratory culture, removed living material, a living organism or a computational model.
records.summary: In vitro and ex vivo describe work outside the original organism, with terminology varying by preparation and expansion. In vivo refers to work within a living organism, including animals and people; in silico refers to computation. Each setting includes different components and omits others. The label does not establish a universal ranking, human safety or treatment benefit.

notes: Setting comparison. In vitro describes laboratory work outside the body, including grown cells and many expanded organoid assays. Ex vivo commonly describes removed living material studied outside its original organism, often briefly with retained local structure. Authors use overlapping terminology, so inspect preparation, expansion and timing. In vivo includes experiments in animals or people; identify species and host. In silico computes a prediction from data rather than directly measuring the predicted response. These terms describe where and how the experiment occurs, not a quality ranking.

Read each omitted compartment. A tumour-only dish lacks required immune interactions unless those populations are added and shown functional. A fresh slice may retain resident neighbours while losing blood flow and recruitment from circulation. A conventional PDX adds mouse circulation, exposure and metabolism without reproducing an intact human immune system. A computational prediction depends on its data, assumptions and benchmark. Human-derived tissue can be used in both dish and animal models; do not claim that ex vivo is the only setting using human tissue. A living specimen can lose cells, adapt or undergo selection after removal; retaining a structure is not retaining complete physiology. In-vitro preparations can isolate direct effects, compare doses and drugs and support repeats, while omitting perfused blood supply, host metabolism and the original population mix unless specifically reconstructed. Latin labels such as in glass, out of the living and in the living are mnemonics for setting, not quality grades.

Primary timing examples. Ladan's breast-slice assay used three-day exposures, a stated planned result window of seven to fourteen days, not a measured turnaround distribution and 23/30 usable tests from tumour-containing biopsies. Izumchenko reported 578/1,163 established PDXs and mean 16 weeks from engraftment to exposure, not biopsy to final decision. Ahlmann-Eltze compared gene-perturbation transcriptome predictions with simple baselines; the deep-learning methods did not outperform the simple linear baselines in the tested expression-prediction tasks. This was not a measured patient drug response. None of these examples shows benefit from choosing a treatment using the model. Sources: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10542784/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5834154/ ; https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40759747/

Terminology scope. NCI's ex vivo dictionary entry describes removal, treatment and return of cells or tissue to the body. That return step distinguishes cell-engineering procedures from laboratory drug testing where the tested sample is not returned. Dosing an animal and later treating removed graft cells in a dish are different experiments. Source: https://www.cancer.gov/publications/dictionaries/cancer-terms/def/ex-vivo

Regulatory scope. FDA's roadmap to reduce animal testing concerns preclinical safety development, initially focusing on monoclonal antibodies and considering human-based laboratory and computational methods. It is not approval of every organ chip or a recommendation for personal treatment selection. Source: https://www.fda.gov/files/newsroom/published/roadmap_to_reducing_animal_testing_in_preclinical_safety_studies.pdf Decision time limits which preparation is usable: establishing a new conventional PDX generally will not fit a decision due in three weeks, while a characterised short-term assay might fit but can still fail. A treatment needing liver activation also needs the relevant metabolic setting represented; a fresh slice alone omits it. Computation can rank hypotheses without growing a model, but a universal fastest or cheapest claim is not established by the setting label.

Fictional reading exercise. Compare a graft dosed in a mouse, a fresh human slice exposed outside the body and a computed sensitivity prediction. Identify actual measurement versus prediction, host, retained cells, omitted physiology and clock before drawing an inference. These settings can start from the same tumour; days, weeks or months are illustrative scales rather than guaranteed timelines. No setting is a later validation rung of another.

An experimental setting and the origin of the material are separate descriptions. Human-derived cells can be studied in vitro, briefly ex vivo or as a graft in vivo. Living-organism work includes animals and people; it does not automatically mean a human clinical trial. Preclinical intervention experiments can continue alongside human studies, so the date relative to a first human dose alone does not validate their treatment claim.

records.name: Minimal / molecular residual disease (MRD)
records.tldr: Residual disease testing looks for small amounts of disease after treatment using a specified sample and method. A negative result means no qualifying signal was detected under that test, rather than proof that no cancer remains.
records.summary: Minimal, measurable and molecular residual disease (MRD) are related terms for small amounts of disease assessed after treatment with a specified method and specimen. Blood-cancer studies can use cell-based or molecular measurements, while solid-tumour studies can look for tumour-associated features in plasma. The disease, specimen, technique, time point and threshold define the result. A negative result means no qualifying signal was detected under that method, not proof that every cancer cell is absent. Associations with recurrence, benefit from a test-guided treatment strategy, and validation of a surrogate endpoint are separate questions; evidence for one setting does not establish the others.

notes: The name has three expansions: minimal residual disease (small remaining amounts), measurable residual disease (used in blood-cancer guidance, stressing what the method can detect) and molecular residual disease (tumour-associated molecular signals after treatment, mostly ctDNA in solid tumours). Check which one a paper means. Cell-frequency thresholds in leukaemia, molecular ratios and plasma detection rules are different quantities, and the European LeukemiaNet update on acute myeloid leukaemia sets disease-specific techniques, materials, time points and thresholds that are not transferable to a solid tumour (Heuser 2021).

Residual disease on a surgical specimen is a different measurement: residual cancer burden is a defined tissue endpoint and is not interchangeable with a blood MRD call. In a fictional study a postoperative plasma test is negative but surgery shows residual invasive cancer. Neither must be wrong, because pathology examined tissue at surgery and the plasma assay sought a qualifying signal in a later blood sample, so dates, specimen and assay limits need reconciling before the pair is read. MRD negative means a method found no qualifying signal in one specimen and not that no cancer cell remains anywhere.

A residual-disease signal can select a research group at higher observed recurrence risk without showing which treatment helps that group. Clinical utility asks whether a test-guided strategy improves a meaningful outcome against an appropriate alternative. Disappearance of a marker is a separate proposed surrogate: it needs validation against the outcome for that setting, rather than becoming proof of cure. These are interpretation distinctions in the FDA November 2024 drug-development guidance, not a universal rule to change treatment.

There is no universal MRD unit or cut-off across diseases and samples. The intended target, background and artefact controls, specimen adequacy and sampling time belong with the call; an unsuitable target or failed preparation must not silently become a negative result. A positive molecular signal does not directly demonstrate a living tumour cell, identify a lesion or guarantee recurrence. The source and the studied clinical context still need to be established.

Read an MRD report by identifying the finite specimen and collection burden first: blood, marrow or another named material. Then name the output, such as a cell percentage, molecular ratio, concentration or assay-defined call, and its disease-specific units and rules. Validation belongs to that disease, treatment setting, specimen, time point and intended decision; a threshold in one combination does not become a universal MRD cut-off.

records.name: Organoid
records.tldr: An organoid is a three-dimensional culture that self-organises selected tissue features. Its measured contents determine which questions it can answer.
records.summary: Organoids self-organise selected structural or functional tissue features in three-dimensional culture. Patient-derived tumour organoids are one member of this broader family, rather than complete copies of a patient. Establishment and growth conditions select cells, and identity and relevant properties need checking against the source specimen. Conventional epithelial cultures often omit immune and supporting populations; specialised retention or added co-cultures require method-specific evidence. Their use for mechanism and drug-response experiments does not by itself establish clinical utility.

notes: Model and assay card. Starting material may be normal tissue, tumour or stem-cell-derived material; retain its source and viable preservation method. Record malignant identity against the specimen, selected or lost populations, matrix/medium, passage and experimental window. Derivation, quality checks, expansion and testing use finite tissue and culture material. A destructive stain or lysate assay consumes its tested aliquot; recovery in another assay is method-specific. No universal specimen amount or organoid-response threshold follows from the name.

Failure and inference checks. Establishment can fail, normal epithelial cells can overgrow malignant cells, and culture conditions can select branches. Verify tumour identity rather than infer it from growth. Output belongs to the chosen assay: attributed cell counts, death-marker fraction or molecular signal, with units, time and normalisation. Check viability, composition, exposure and controls. A three-dimensional spheroid need not show tissue-like self-organisation, and specialised immune retention does not apply to all cultures. Sources: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30550791/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10598932/ Dijkstra explicitly checked tumour identity to exclude healthy-lung organoid overgrowth: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6558289/

Size, matrix, oxygen supply and exposure duration belong in the experiment record because they define conditions for delivery, cell state and the readout. As a bounded example, Geyer's pancreatic organoid study found treatment-response differences between normoxia and hypoxia in specified monocultures and co-cultures. Treat size as a geometry and exposure-control question rather than assume equal supply across differently sized structures. Source: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41420-023-01334-z

DeStefanis and colleagues tracked nearly 3,500 individual mouse-derived colon-cancer organoids. In that model, organoids at or above a change point of about 308 micrometres at baseline grew more slowly, and individual-organoid tracking was reported to be more sensitive to treatment response than well-level assessment, which averages the whole population in a well. In their 1,740 patient-derived organoids (22 lines, 19 patients) they found no relation between baseline size and growth (R squared 0.023) and no change point in any line. These are findings of one study and model, not a universal size threshold. Source: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-022-08937-z

Fictional reading exercise. An epithelial organoid loses T cells and has lower metabolic signal after treatment. The signal does not establish immune-mediated killing. Adding immune cells creates a new experiment needing identity, persistence and specificity controls. The model can support a direct tumour-cell question while leaving host exposure, organ toxicity and patient benefit untested.

The word organoid establishes no regulatory status or clinical authorisation. Sachs's breast-cancer biobank generated characterised lines and reported retention of many source features during extended passaging; that supports a particular culture resource, not every preparation or personal treatment prediction. Source: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2017.11.010

records.name: Patient-derived organoids
records.tldr: Patient-derived tumour organoids are cultures that self-organise selected tissue features and support defined laboratory experiments.
records.summary: Patient-derived tumour organoids are cultures established from a patient's tumour tissue that can be expanded for repeated laboratory experiments when establishment succeeds. They are one member of the broader organoid family defined on the organoid record; establishment selects cells, malignant identity must be checked against the source specimen, and conventional epithelial cultures usually lack immune and supporting populations. Mechanism and drug-response results from them do not by themselves establish clinical utility.

notes: Patient-derived organoids can provide expandable material for repeated experiments when establishment succeeds. They are one part of the broader organoid family. The organoid definition holds the shared construction, consumption, quality-control and readout explanation; the technology record concerns their use as a research resource. A successful culture still needs malignant-cell identity and intended-use checks. Sources: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2017.11.010 ; https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2018.11.021

Drug-specific agreement can fail to transfer even within colorectal cancer. Ooft and colleagues reported that organoids predicted the biopsied lesion's response in more than 80 percent of people receiving irinotecan-based treatment, but failed to predict response to fluorouracil plus oxaliplatin. The Netherlands Cancer Institute's 2019 research announcement describes 61 patients in the clinical study; Wensink's later review tabulates 29 people in the response-comparison cohort, including ten receiving irinotecan and twelve receiving an irinotecan doublet. Those cohort and regimen denominators are not interchangeable. This was a prediction comparison, not evidence that assigning treatment by the test improved patient outcomes.

Wensink's 2021 review included seventeen publications, five about colorectal cancer; seven used metastatic populations. Its pooled sensitivity was 81 percent and specificity 74 percent for the included response comparisons. The authors warned that these estimates were likely high because some studies lacked quantitative results needed for pooling and not all used a predefined index test; publication or outcome-reporting bias could not be excluded. The pooled establishment estimate was 68.0 percent at patient level and 68.5 percent at sample level, with heterogeneous studies and wide intervals. These are different quantities from response agreement and from clinical utility. The review also reports a 34-day median just to establish organoids from breast biopsies, distinct from a completed drug panel or an individual decision deadline.

Vlachogiannis and colleagues studied organoids from heavily pretreated metastatic colorectal and gastroesophageal cancers. They grew organoids from 70 percent of adequately cellular biopsies and compared model and clinical drug responses in 21 comparisons. The reported sensitivity was 100 percent, specificity 93 percent, positive predictive value 88 percent and negative predictive value 100 percent for those comparisons. These are the study's response metrics with its defined comparators and selected denominator, not 88 percent accuracy for all patients or evidence for a postoperative breast decision. Culture success, response agreement and benefit from assigning treatment remain separate questions.

Boileve and colleagues prospectively enrolled 87 people with pretreated advanced pancreatic cancer, generated 54 organoids (62 percent) and had 34 evaluable patients with clinical follow-up. The 34 evaluable people are about 39 percent of the original 87, not 39 percent of successful cultures. Mean time to a chemogram was 6.8 weeks; reported sensitivity was 83.3 percent and specificity 92.9 percent. Those selected results and routine-care hit versus nonhit comparisons do not establish a randomised treatment-selection benefit or validate a breast-cancer assay.

Colorectal cancer: Bertotti and colleagues used xenografts from 85 metastatic colorectal cancer samples and found HER2 amplification in a subset of cetuximab-resistant cases (2011). The abstract describes xenografts, not organoids, and does not establish priority before every clinical trial. Calon and colleagues reported that TGF-beta signalling inhibitors blocked cancer-microenvironment cross-talk and halted disease progression in patient-derived organoid and xenograft experiments (2015). Sources: https://doi.org/10.1158/2159-8290.CD-11-0109 ; https://doi.org/10.1038/ng.3225
records.principle: Culture viable source cells in a specified environment, then verify the selected tissue features and assay response.
strengths: Material for repeated controlled experiments when establishment succeeds
limitations: Selection, normal-cell overgrowth and culture changes require checks
Conventional preparations do not recreate complete host physiology
Patient prediction and clinical utility need intended-use evidence

records.name: Patient-derived xenografts
records.tldr: A patient-derived xenograft is patient tumour material grown in another species, commonly a mouse, for experiments under whole-animal exposure.
records.summary: A patient-derived xenograft starts with patient tumour material implanted into another species, commonly an immunodeficient mouse. It can retain relevant tumour features within a different host, while engraftment selects populations and mouse-derived support can replace human stroma and vessels. Whole-animal dosing includes mouse exposure and metabolism, not human physiology. Humanised models add selected components whose identity, compatibility and persistence need checking. Fidelity and patient prediction are question- and method-specific.

Ben-David reported mouse-specific copy-number evolution in studied datasets; Woo's direct-DNA analyses reported conservation and showed that measurement method matters. Assay card. Viable material, establishment, passage and animal experiments consume finite material. Report burden or volume with units, baseline and observation clock, exposure and comparator animals, and donor versus animal counts. Failed engraftment and excluded experiments remain visible. Human-specific binding to tumour cells does not establish activity on mouse stromal targets. A graft tested later in a dish has a different experimental setting. Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3553601/

A fictional example separates denominators: ten donor specimens are submitted, four establish grafts, three yield an interpretable drug experiment and two meet its response criterion. Establishment is 4/10; response among interpretable donor models is 2/3, not a patient-response rate. A human-specific antibody binding a retained tumour receptor also does not establish binding to mouse-derived vessel targets required by a proposed mechanism.

NCI's model repository uses lineage identity, pathology and human/mouse-content checks and notes that some models evolve with passage. Its procedures and material types are repository-specific. Yang's 2026 primary abstract describes adding patient-derived tumour and mesenchymal cells, human endothelial cells and humanised marrow to a specialised immune-stroma PDX. This is evidence for a defined added-component model, not complete reconstruction of human immunity. Sources: https://dctd.cancer.gov/drug-discovery-development/reagents-materials/pdmr/models ; https://doi.org/10.1007/s00262-026-04349-4

Izumchenko and colleagues compared 129 treatments across 92 people with advanced solid tumours. Their 112/129 agreement figure (87 percent) grouped stable disease with partial and complete responses as positive disease control; reported sensitivity was 96 percent and specificity 70 percent. Requiring the exact RECIST category instead gave 91/129 agreement (71 percent). Responses came from the consulting oncologist and from xenograft volume changes converted to RECIST equivalents. These selected, repeated treatment comparisons are not 129 independent people, a head-to-head accuracy ranking against other model types or a trial showing benefit from assigning treatment by the model.

strengths: Can assess selected source-tumour features over time
limitations: Engraftment can fail and favours some tumours: Hidalgo describes a general impression that more aggressive tumours engraft more often (for example hormone-receptor-negative more than hormone-sensitive breast tumours), so collections can over-represent them; take rate varies by tumour type
Mouse support, metabolism and immunity differ from human care
Establishment and testing can take months

records.name: Pharmacokinetics (PK), half-life and exposure
records.tldr: Pharmacokinetics follows a named medicine or its components through the body by measuring concentration over time, which differs from both the amount administered and the biological effect.
records.summary:
Pharmacokinetics describes absorption, distribution, metabolism and excretion. A dose is an administered amount; exposure describes a named substance's concentration over time in a specified compartment. Route, organ function, metabolism, binding and interactions can make equal doses produce different exposure.

The December 2016 FDA labelling guidance asks for measures such as maximum plasma concentration, concentration-time area under the curve, clearance, accumulation and half-life in their relevant conditions. These measurements inform dosage selection alongside activity, safety and tolerability; they do not establish benefit on their own. For conjugated drugs, active metabolites and radiopharmaceuticals, specify which component was measured. Blood concentration is not automatically the concentration of active material at a cancer-cell target.

notes: Dose, exposure and effect are three different things. Dose is the administered amount; exposure is a named substance's concentration over time in a named place, which route, organ function, interactions and product properties can change for the same dose; and effect is a separate measurement, because effects or injury can persist after exposure falls and detectable drug does not guarantee productive engagement. Pharmacokinetics follows absorption (including how much of an oral dose reaches the circulation), distribution (plasma is not the unbound concentration inside a cell), metabolism (active metabolites may add their own exposure) and excretion, summarised by clearance, the removal relative to concentration, in volume per time. FDA labelling guidance lists the maximum plasma concentration (Cmax) and area under the concentration-time curve (AUC) at the approved dosage, time to steady state, accumulation ratio, clearance, volume of distribution and half-life; this AUC is an exposure area and is unrelated to the area under a prediction curve that judges tests.

For an antibody-drug conjugate, specify whether an assay follows conjugated antibody, total antibody, unconjugated payload or an active breakdown product. The 2024 FDA guidance defines total antibody as antibody with or without attached payload and discusses relevant constituent parts, metabolites and catabolites. Their concentration histories can differ: persistent antibody signal does not establish active payload in every cancer cell. Living cell products can expand or persist, and a radioligand combines radioactive decay with biological removal, so a freely circulating drug's half-life gives no universal clock for them.

Read the measurement card as well as the curve. Record the dose, route, analyte, sampled compartment, assay, population and sampling interval. Concentration can be in ng/mL, maximum concentration in the same units, concentration-time area in ng·hour/mL, half-life in hours and clearance in litres per hour. Sampling should capture the phase of interest: a sparse late sample cannot reliably recover an unobserved early peak. Pharmacodynamics measures biological effects separately. First-pass metabolism can reduce oral bioavailability; protein binding and active metabolites also matter.

The fictional halving example assumes one compartment, stopped input and a constant four-hour half-life. Its four markers are model values, not observed samples: 100, 50, 25 and 12.5 ng/mL at 0, 4, 8 and 12 hours. Integrating that exponential only from 0 to 12 hours gives about 505 ng·hour/mL, not the lifetime area, administered dose or biological effect. The example supplies no safe next-treatment time.

A fictional six-month research plan measures neither a batch's manufacturing lead time nor the duration of drug action. Designing and testing a candidate, making and quality-releasing a specified batch, and observing exposure and effects after dosing are three different clocks. A laboratory binder may never become a clinically usable product. Ask separately whether material is ready, a clinical use is authorised, eligibility is met and an appropriate site can provide it; a calendar estimate does not answer those questions. Repeated protein doses and preparation of a person's cell product are different tasks. Research dependencies can overlap without establishing that concurrent treatments are effective, safe or authorised. For the dosing clock, ask which schedule and monitoring are supported for the actual product and setting.

records.name: Positive predictive value (PPV)
records.tldr: Positive predictive value is the fraction of positive results that match the reference condition rather than being false positive calls. It depends on prevalence and the test's actual performance.
records.summary: Positive predictive value is the proportion of positive test calls that meet a specified reference condition: true positives divided by true plus false positives. A positive result can be a true positive or a false positive; a false positive is a positive call in someone without that reference condition. Negative predictive value uses negative calls as its denominator. These differ from sensitivity and specificity, which start with reference-condition groups. The population base rate, reference standard, threshold and actual assay performance determine how the fractions should be interpreted.

links.label: Wikipedia
FDA: statistical guidance for reporting diagnostic-test studies

notes: Separate the index-test result from a defined reference condition. Sensitivity is TP/(TP+FN), the positive fraction among reference cases; specificity is TN/(TN+FP), the negative fraction among reference non-cases. PPV is TP/(TP+FP), the reference-case fraction among positive calls; NPV is TN/(TN+FN), the reference-noncase fraction among negative calls. Base rate means prevalence of that reference condition in the intended tested population. Regrouping the same people by positive calls changes a denominator without adding participants.

Fictional groups each contain 1,000 people, with complete reference assessment, no indeterminate results and assumed sensitivity 80 per cent and specificity 90 per cent. At 10 per cent prevalence there are TP 80, FN 20, FP 90 and TN 810: PPV is 80/170, about 47.1 per cent, and NPV 810/830, about 97.6 per cent. At 50 per cent prevalence the counts are 400, 100, 50 and 450: PPV is 88.9 and NPV 81.8 per cent. At 5 per cent prevalence there are 40 true and 95 false positive calls, giving PPV 29.6 per cent. The examples hold performance fixed to isolate base rate; real populations can change performance too. High NPV can coexist with missed cases and is not a universal absence-of-disease guarantee.

Use test results and suitable independent reference outcomes in the intended population. Keep the locked threshold, condition definition, assay version, all four counts, confidence intervals and handling of missing or indeterminate results. Verifying only positive calls, using an imperfect comparator or borrowing another population's prevalence can mislead. Without a reference that establishes the condition, positive and negative percent agreement may be the appropriate descriptions; agreement does not prove either method correct. Imaging and pathological response are different assessments, so a comparison needs the population, regimen, definition, timing and surgical reference. Accuracy alone establishes neither treatment benefit nor safe surgery omission, and population fractions are not automatic personal probabilities.

Fictional examples hold sensitivity at 90 per cent and specificity at 95 per cent to isolate the base rate, with complete reference assessment and no indeterminate tests. Among 1,000 people with condition prevalence 10 per cent, 100 have the condition: 90 test positive, while 45 of the 900 without it test positive. PPV is 90/(90 + 45), about 67 per cent. At 2 per cent prevalence, 20 have the condition: 18 test positive and 49 of the other 980 test positive. PPV is 18/(18 + 49), about 27 per cent. The same assumed sensitivity and specificity therefore yield very different positive-call fractions. Actual performance can also change across populations. A negative test retains its detection limits, specimen timing and pretest context rather than guaranteeing absence of disease.

records.name: Randomised trial
records.tldr: A study that assigns eligible participants to interventions by chance. This reduces treatment-selection bias but does not guarantee identical groups, flawless follow-up or benefit.
records.summary: A randomized trial assigns eligible consenting participants to interventions by chance. Concealing the next assignment protects enrolment against foreknowledge; blinding concerns awareness after assignment. These are different design features. Randomization reduces treatment-selection confounding but leaves possible chance imbalance, missing outcomes and limits on applicability. The comparator, endpoint, analysis and conduct determine what the comparison establishes.

notes: Concealed chance assignment is different from predictable alternation between A and B. Allocation concealment hides the next assignment during enrolment; blinding concerns who knows the assigned treatment afterwards and may not be feasible for every intervention. Report sequence generation, allocation, who was blinded, assigned-group analyses, exclusions, dropout, missing assessments, treatment changes and unequal follow-up. Chance can balance measured and unmeasured factors on average without guaranteeing identical groups in one trial. Random assignment is not random sampling from a population: consenting eligible volunteers remain selected.

Controls can be standard care, standard care plus placebo or another protocol-defined option, not automatically no treatment. A fictional single-group Drug A study showing shrinkage supports an activity question for further study; it does not isolate added survival benefit from selection, natural history and other care. A randomized A-plus-usual-care versus usual-care comparison can test the added effect under sound conduct and analysis, while a volunteer cannot choose their randomized assignment or be promised benefit. A chance-assigned two-group phase 2 trial is randomized even though it is not phase 3.

records.name: RECIST
records.tldr: RECIST 1.1 uses predefined anatomical measurements and other disease findings to classify response. A target sum is not every cancer site or total tumour volume.
records.summary:
RECIST 1.1 selects up to five measurable target lesions, with at most two per organ. Ordinary lesions contribute longest diameters; qualifying lymph nodes contribute short-axis measurements. Other disease is recorded separately, along with new lesions. The target sum is a selected measurement, rather than a complete inventory or volume of cancer.

For target lesions, partial response requires at least a 30 percent decrease from the baseline sum. Progression requires at least a 20 percent increase from the smallest sum on study, together with at least a five-millimetre absolute increase. Baseline is the progression reference if it remains the smallest sum. Unequivocal non-target progression or an unequivocal new malignant lesion can change the overall category despite shrinking targets.

Overall complete response requires the applicable target, non-target and new-lesion conditions, including short-axis reduction below ten millimetres for pathological nodes. Missing or equivocal findings require the protocol’s handling. Confirmation of response is not mandatory in every design: the guideline requires it for non-randomised trials whose primary endpoint is response.

Record the framework/version, selected lesions, dates, baseline, nadir, current values, acquisition comparability and findings outside the sum. iRECIST and metabolic PET criteria add different rules; an anatomical response does not establish tissue clearance, cure or a treatment decision.

notes: In a fictional target-sum sequence of 100, 60 and 73 millimetres, the last value is 27 percent below baseline but 13 millimetres, about 21.7 percent, above nadir. Under the stated assumption of comparable measurements and no outside progression, it meets both target-progression increases. This arithmetic is not a clinical decision rule for an unassessed person.

records.name: Single-cell mass and growth-rate assays
records.tldr: Repeated calibrated mass measurements can estimate a cell's growth rate; slower mass accumulation does not by itself show cell death.
records.summary: A suspended microchannel resonator weighs a cell relative to the fluid it displaces using the shift in a vibrating beam's frequency. Buoyant mass equals cell volume multiplied by the difference between cell and fluid density. It is not simply diameter or dry mass. Repeatedly measuring the same cell estimates mass accumulation rate; Godin reversed the flow to reintroduce the same cell to the sensor (a dynamic trap) and Cermak used serial sensors along one channel. Stevens investigated drug-response associations in specified cancer models and leukaemia samples, rather than universal clinical prediction.

notes: Assay card. Input: viable cells compatible with suspension and channel handling. Record source, identity, preparation losses, fluid and temperature conditions, exposure and observation interval. Calibration maps frequency shifts to mass, often picograms. Tracking repeated readings estimates a slope, often picograms per hour; mass-normalised rates have inverse-time units. Preparation and exposure consume finite material; the physical measurement can preserve cells, but recovery and downstream compatibility depend on the method.

Quality and inference. Check clumps, cell attribution, instrument drift, calibration, tracking ambiguity and sufficient linked readings. Serial-sensor analyses exclude uncertain matches rather than invent a trajectory. Fluid-density changes can change buoyant mass. A small positive slope still indicates accumulation in the observed interval; later recovery, death and resistance need additional endpoints and time. Many measured cells from one specimen are not many independent patients. No universal rate cutoff establishes clinical sensitivity or immune recognition. Buoyant mass is also not a count of cell divisions. Physical measurement performance, a reproducible drug-response association and validated use for a clinical decision are separate kinds of evidence. Without extra measurements or assumptions, this sensor does not establish dry mass, a death mechanism, immune specificity or patient benefit.

Fictional arithmetic. A tracked cell rising from 10 to 12 picograms over one hour has a slope of 2 picograms per hour. Comparable groups at 2 and 0.5 picograms per hour differ by (2 minus 0.5) divided by 2, or 75 percent. Both rates are positive. This is a rate reduction, not shrinkage, a killed-cell fraction or patient response. These values are invented.

The positive research use is a rapid physical response readout and a view of cell-to-cell variation that a population average can conceal. Stevens measured short-term mass accumulation in specified cancer models and leukaemia samples; this can precede a large endpoint-count change, while slower accumulation can occur in living cells. A mixed specimen still requires attribution to the relevant population, and a mass sensor does not supply immune cells or recognition. Sources: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5142231/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5064867/
records.principle: Calibrate a frequency shift to buoyant mass and track repeated readings from the same cell to estimate mass accumulation rate.

records.name: Surrogate endpoint validation: which stand-ins have earned trust
records.tldr: A surrogate endpoint only deserves trust if trials have shown that moving it moves the outcome that matters, in that disease and for that kind of drug; some stand-ins have passed that test, several have not, and the record differs endpoint by endpoint.
records.summary:
A marker can be associated with a later outcome without being validated as a substitute for it. For treatment-effect surrogacy, the question is whether changes caused by treatment in the proposed surrogate predict changes in the outcome of interest. Trial-level validation examines treatment effects across suitable randomised studies, with attention to disease, treatment class, endpoint and intended outcome. A patient-level association alone cannot establish that relationship.

Named examples require their own population, regimen and analysis. In the final TROPION-Breast01 analysis of previously treated hormone-receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer, overall survival was not statistically significantly improved (hazard ratio 1.01, 95% confidence interval 0.83 to 1.22); this does not establish exactly zero effect. Later antibody-drug-conjugate use was imbalanced between arms (12.3% with datopotamab deruxtecan and 24.0% with chemotherapy); the authors note that it may have affected the survival result. DUO-O met its progression-free-survival endpoints for a specified multi-drug strategy in newly diagnosed non-BRCA-mutated advanced ovarian cancer, while the reported overall-survival analysis was interim at 39% maturity. BEAT-meso tested adding atezolizumab to bevacizumab and chemotherapy in advanced pleural mesothelioma: progression-free survival improved, while its primary overall-survival comparison did not meet statistical significance. These are distinct comparisons, rather than interchangeable evidence that progression-free survival cannot matter.

Olaratumab is not an example of approval resting on response rate alone. FDA's 2016 review described an uncertain survival estimate from a small randomised study as central to accelerated approval and did not regard its response-rate effect as clinically meaningful. ANNOUNCE subsequently did not confirm the survival benefit. Lurbinectedin's 2020 accelerated approval instead relied on response rate and duration of response. ATLANTIS tested lower-dose lurbinectedin combined with doxorubicin against chemotherapy in relapsed small-cell lung cancer; it did not demonstrate a statistically significant survival improvement. That result must retain its combination, dose and comparator rather than being described as a test of the approved monotherapy regimen.

For a trial that improves a surrogate, ask whether trial-level validation applies to this disease, treatment class and intended outcome. Read the clinical-outcome estimate and its uncertainty for benefit and harm compatible with the data, and check the status of any required confirmatory trial. A nonsignificant survival comparison alone establishes neither equivalence nor absence of harm.

Other linked records include CodeBreaK 200, adjuvant trials, residual-disease trials and UKCTOCS screening. They remain related studies, rather than interchangeable validation of a surrogate. This account does not reassert their previously listed outcome or regulatory-validation claims, which require source-specific verification. The linked trial-design bottleneck and proposal for independent surrogate validation extend the methodological questions.

notes: A surrogate is a measured outcome used in place of a direct clinical-benefit outcome, with evidence needed for that substitution in the intended setting. Two relationships must be separated: people with a favourable marker may have better outcomes, while treatments that improve that marker may or may not improve the outcome. The first is a prognostic association; the second concerns agreement between treatment effects across suitable randomised comparisons. A treatment can change another pathway, later disease or toxicity as well as the marker. Validation is specific to disease, treatment context and intended outcome. An early measure is not automatically validated, and regulatory acceptance in one programme does not transfer to another. “Validated” and “reasonably likely to predict benefit” carry different evidence claims. Even a pathology or imaging response does not capture every benefit and harm.

Imagine twenty fictional people grouped by whether they achieved pathological complete response, with complete event follow-up to three years. A difference in events between those groups would describe an association after response was achieved, rather than preserve a randomised treatment comparison. Across six fictional randomised trials, a different analysis would compare each trial's treatment-related gain in response with its gain in three-year event-free survival, both in percentage points. Those are different units of evidence; neither constructed example is the CTNeoBC dataset. Similarly, a fictional trial increasing complete response from 40/100 to 55/100 establishes a 15-percentage-point response difference under its definition, with uncertainty still needed. Immature survival follow-up does not supply a proven survival gain.

Pathological complete response is assessed in the surgical specimen after neoadjuvant treatment, rather than a presurgical scan or biopsy. Retain the exact definition, such as ypT0/Tis ypN0 meaning no invasive disease in breast or nodes, and how missing surgery or specimens affect denominators. CTNeoBC pooled 11,955 people from 12 trials: achieving that response was associated with event-free-survival HR 0.48 and overall-survival HR 0.36; corresponding triple-negative subgroup estimates were 0.24 and 0.16. Yet trial-level R-squared was 0.03 for event-free survival (95% interval 0.00 to 0.25) and 0.24 for overall survival (0.00 to 0.70). Conforti and colleagues' analysis of 54 trials and 32,611 participants found R-squared 0.14 (95% interval 0.00 to 0.29) for disease-free and 0.08 (0.00 to 0.22) for overall survival. R-squared here is the share of variation in the treatment effects on survival that is explained by the treatment effects on pathological complete response; 1 would be a perfect fit. Thus response can be strongly associated with outcomes among participants while remaining a weak substitute for treatment effects across trials. This fitted association is not an individually validated risk prediction. These fitted associations concern variation in treatment effects across trials, with substantial uncertainty; they are not personal prognosis models.

A weak trial-level association does not mean no regimen can improve both endpoints. KEYNOTE-522 reported a 13.6-percentage-point pathological-response gain and subsequently event-free and overall-survival gains, each in its own analysis. One regimen's success does not validate the surrogate across regimens. For every comparison, retain population, intervention, comparator, assessment time and response uncertainty, then separately the survival event definition, starting clock and follow-up. A response association and a demonstrated treatment benefit remain different claims.

records.name: Tumour-on-a-chip
records.tldr: A tumour-on-chip is an engineered culture device for studying selected tumour interactions under specified physical and biological conditions.
records.summary: Chip devices can control selected cells, matrix, interfaces, transport or mechanical conditions. Their composition varies: channels do not automatically supply endothelium or immune cells. Huh's lung model separated alveolar and vascular compartments and imposed mechanical strain; Hassell studied lung cancer in defined engineered environments. Jenkins placed immune-containing organotypic spheroids in a collagen microfluidic compartment. These are capabilities of particular systems, not universal chip properties or validation for personal treatment selection.

notes: Geometry and exposure. A porous interface, a perfused channel and a tissue compartment are separate features. In Huh's design, a membrane separated epithelial and endothelial layers and vacuum channels imposed deformation. Jenkins used collagen containing spheroids in a central channel. These geometries must not be silently interchanged. A fictional one-micromolar inlet illustrates a reading rule: concentration at an inlet is not a measurement at each cell. Sources: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8335790/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5809290/ One micromolar means one micromole per litre; it is the nominal inlet value in this example, not a measured cellular exposure.

Model and assay card. Record viable cell/tissue sources, matrix, channel geometry, material, flow or exchange conditions, barrier performance, loading losses and quality window. Preparation, loading and endpoint assays use finite material. Report the actual endpoint and units: attributed counts or death, permeability, cytokine concentration or motion, with time and denominator. Verify initial composition, baseline survival and local exposure; incompatible materials, unequal delivery and poor barriers can confound results. Device and assay acceptance criteria are method-specific. A chip may combine bioprinting, organoids or co-culture without recreating complete circulation. Microfluidics controls fluid in small channels. Perfusion supplies fluid through a system; it does not itself recreate human circulation or prove a functional vascular lining. Immune cells, if present, still need recognition and attribution controls. A tumour-on-chip is a living experimental device, whereas an in-silico model computes predictions. A device without the required immune cells cannot test their checkpoint interaction. Cells can alter the engineered environment, so both the design and its measured biological state matter; added detail alone does not establish better prediction.

In Hassell's defined lung-cancer chip systems, breathing-related physical cues affected growth, invasion and responses to tyrosine kinase inhibitors. This is a context-dependent experimental finding, not a claim that every chip reproduces a whole organ or predicts all cancers. Jenkins described spheroids retaining autologous immune and stromal components in a collagen channel, with components and windows tied to that protocol. Sources: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.celrep.2017.09.043 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5809290/
records.principle: Characterise the chosen geometry, components and conditions, then measure the response with matched controls.
strengths: Control over selected physical and biological interactions
Can examine transport or mechanical effects in a defined setting
limitations: Geometry, composition and exposure require measurement
Material and delivery effects can confound biological interpretation
Does not reproduce whole-body physiology or establish clinical utility

records.name: Virtual cell models and in-silico perturbation screens
records.tldr: A virtual cell is a computer model of specified aspects of cells. A predicted response is a model output whose accuracy must be tested against independent measurements.
records.summary: A virtual cell is a computational model of specified aspects of cells. Its outputs and evaluation depend on the task, training data and model version. scGen combined variational autoencoders with latent-space vector arithmetic and was reported to model perturbation and infection responses across cell types, studies and species, having noted that generalisation to phenomena absent from training data had not previously been shown (Lotfollahi and colleagues, 2019). A 2025 benchmark found that none of five single-cell foundation models and two other deep-learning models predicted transcriptome changes after single or double gene perturbations better than deliberately simple baselines; for most genes the predictions of scGPT, UCE and scBERT did not vary across perturbations, and those of GEARS and scFoundation varied considerably less than the observed values (Ahlmann-Eltze and colleagues, 2025). An AI virtual cell is described as a multi-scale, multi-modal large neural network model in a perspective that sets priorities for accelerating discoveries and guiding experiments, not a validation (Bunne and colleagues, 2024).

notes: Reading guide (OnCo inference). The task defines what an output means: filling a missing RNA value from an image, estimating a drug response and predicting a gene-disruption response are different tasks, and success at one does not validate another. A virtual perturbation changes a model input and calculates an output; it is not a performed experiment, and masking a gene value is not the same as removing the gene's function. Predicted RNA is not measured RNA, protein activity or patient benefit. Agreement summarised across all genes can conceal poor prediction of the few genes that changed, so compare against simple baselines on the genes that moved. An association learned from untreated tissue does not by itself identify a causal drug effect. Whether a model's output supports treatment selection needs separate intended-use clinical evidence, whereas prioritising experiments is a lesser claim.

Fictional worked example. A model accurately fills missing RNA values from images of familiar samples. That is measurement completion; it says nothing about a drug that was never tested. To claim a drug response, define the intervention and outcome, reserve independent measured experiments, and compare with baselines and the measured response.

Fictional worked example. A model learns RNA responses to interventions in one cell line and correctly predicts additional cells exposed to a familiar intervention. That did not test a never-tested intervention in breast tumour cells; a reserved set of measured interventions and compatible breast-cell data would support a closer evaluation.

Model card in words (a reading guide). Input and tissue cost: the measured data, preprocessing and missing inputs; computation uses data, while new data collection may consume tissue. Output: the predicted object with units, intervention, dose and time. Version and scope: model version, training population and intended task. Evaluation: what was held out, the baselines, error measures and external data. Failure modes: leakage, incompatible inputs, context shift or the wrong endpoint. Cannot establish alone: a performed perturbation, complete cell biology or better clinical outcomes.

Figure reading (fictional teaching scene, light and dark renders agree): panel 1 fills a missing observation, where images paired with RNA from a defined population train a model that outputs a computed RNA value for a held-out donor and is tested against the masked measured value; panel 2 trains on measured responses to familiar X and forecasts withheld Y, tested later against a reserved measured response; panel 3 says a new donor tests donor generalisation, a new intervention tests intervention transfer, and neither automatically tests a new cell type. Computed is not measured, and the population, task and version stay attached.

The original model-choice exercise stipulates a fictional virtual-C-v1 model: compatible measured expression data go in, and normalised RNA expression 48 hours after gene C disruption is predicted. No physical drug exposure occurred. Compare unperturbed or no-change baselines with independently measured responses in reserved new donors and the withheld C intervention. All fitting, threshold and preprocessing choices belong to development. A new donor tests a different transfer question from a new perturbation, cell type or laboratory. This computational result can prioritise a measured experiment; it supplies neither protein effects, immune interactions, safe delivery nor clinical benefit.
